Preparing your data

Source: vignettes/preparing-data.Rmd
preparing-data.Rmd

This guide describes the file cd2030.core reads, what happens to it when it is loaded, and how to find out what is wrong with a file that does not load.

library(cd2030.core)
path <- system.file("extdata", "kenya.xlsx", package = "cd2030.core")

The three kinds of file

File What it is Read with
.xlsx, .xls The Countdown workbook, one sheet per kind of data load_data(), load_cache_data()
.dta A Stata master file: the merged table, already one row per district and month load_data(), load_cache_data()
.rds A dataset saved by this package, with the choices made about it load_cache_data()

The workbook

The example workbook has these sheets:

readxl::excel_sheets(path)
#>  [1] "Read_me"                "Data_checks"            "Admin_data"            
#>  [4] "Population_data"        "Reporting_completeness" "Service_data_1"        
#>  [7] "Service_data_2"         "Service_data_3"         "Vaccine_stock_data"    
#> [10] "Contextual_campaigns"

Four kinds of sheet are read. The others (the read-me, the workbook’s own checks, stock and campaign data) are left alone.

Sheet One row per Key columns Holds
Admin_data district district the country, the first administrative level (region) of each district, numbers of facilities and staff
Population_data district and year district, year total population, under-fives, under-ones, live births, total births, women aged 15 to 49
Reporting_completeness district and month district, year, month reports expected and received, and the reporting rate, for each group of services
Service_data_1, Service_data_2, … district and month district, year, month the monthly counts: one column per indicator

Every sheet whose name contains Service_data is read, so indicators can be spread over as many service sheets as is convenient. If your workbook names its sheets differently, give the names:

load_data(
  "my-country.xlsx",
  admin_sheet_name = "Admin",
  population_sheet_name = "Population",
  reporting_sheet_name = "Completeness",
  service_sheet_names = c("ANC", "Delivery", "Vaccines")
)

What loading does 

data <- load_data(path)
#> ℹ Loading Excel "kenya.xlsx" for parts
#> ! The following columns are empty: anc_1trimester, under5_deaths, total_deaths, ipv2, measles_cases
#> ℹ Successfully loaded and cleaned data
#> ℹ Auto-detect candidates (|group|): vaccine=19, rmncah=28 -> selected rmncah
  1. Column names are cleaned: lower case, with the workbook’s headings mapped to the names the package uses (First_admin_level becomes adminlevel_1, Penta1 becomes penta1).
  2. The sheets are merged into one table with a row for each district and month.
  3. The country is recognised from the Admin sheet, and its ISO3 code is attached. The name can be any usual form of it ("Kenya", "Republic of Kenya", "KEN", "RDC", "Côte d'Ivoire", "Ivory Coast"), whatever the case or accents, and a small misspelling is accepted. A name that could be two countries stops the load and names both. The country must be one of those the package holds reference data for.
  4. The indicator group is detected: the group whose indicators best match the columns in the file.
  5. Empty columns are reported, as in the message above. They are not an error: an indicator your country does not collect stays empty and its results are left out.

The result is a tibble of class cd_data. The country and group travel with it:

attr(data, "country")
#> [1] "Kenya"
attr(data, "iso3")
#> [1] "KEN"
attr(data, "indicator_group")
#> [1] "rmncah"

Indicator groups

An indicator group says which indicators a dataset has and how they are grouped for reporting rates and adjustment. Two are built in.

list_indicator_groups()
#> [1] "rmncah"  "vaccine"

These are the groups and indicators of the one the example file was matched to:

get_indicator_groups()
#> $anc
#> [1] "anc1"           "anc_1trimester" "anc4"           "ipt2"           "ipt3"          
#> [6] "syphilis_test"  "ifa90"          "hiv_test"      
#> 
#> $idelv
#>  [1] "sba"              "ideliv"           "instlivebirths"   "csection"         "low_bweight"     
#>  [6] "pnc48h"           "total_stillbirth" "stillbirth_f"     "stillbirth_m"     "maternal_deaths" 
#> [11] "neonatal_deaths" 
#> 
#> $vacc
#> [1] "penta1"   "penta3"   "measles1" "measles2" "bcg"     
#> 
#> $opd
#> [1] "opd_total"  "opd_under5"
#> 
#> $ipd
#> [1] "ipd_total"  "ipd_under5"

A group of indicators has a reporting rate column named after it (anc_rr, idelv_rr, vacc_rr, opd_rr), which is what the Reporting_completeness sheet supplies.

To load a file as a particular group, name it: load_data(path, indicator_group = "vaccine"). To add indicators of your own to a built-in group, register them before loading:

register_indicator_group("rmncah", list(hiv = c("hiv_test", "pmtct1")), on_conflict = "merge")

What the columns mean

cd_dictionary() holds the package’s vocabulary: the indicators, the populations, the denominators and the pattern of the computed column names.

head(cd_dictionary()$indicators)
#>               id             label group computed
#> 1           anc1             ANC 1   anc    FALSE
#> 2 anc_1trimester ANC 1st Trimester   anc    FALSE
#> 3           anc4      ANC 4 Visits   anc    FALSE
#> 4           ipt2      IPT 2nd Dose   anc    FALSE
#> 5           ipt3      IPT 3rd Dose   anc    FALSE
#> 6  syphilis_test     Syphilis Test   anc    FALSE

cd_describe_columns() explains any column name, including the computed ones that appear later in the analysis.

cd_describe_columns(c("anc1", "vacc_rr", "cov_penta3_dhis2", "totunder1_un"))[, c("column", "type", "description")]
#>             column           type
#> 1             anc1          count
#> 2          vacc_rr reporting_rate
#> 3 cov_penta3_dhis2       coverage
#> 4     totunder1_un     population
#>                                                                       description
#> 1                                                         ANC 1 (number reported)
#> 2                    Reporting rate, vaccination (% of expected reports received)
#> 3           Coverage of Pentavalent 3 (%), denominator: DHIS2 projections (dhis2)
#> 4 Children under 1 (thousands) estimated with the UN projections denominator (un)

When a file does not load

load_data() stops with a message when the file cannot be used. The usual causes:

  • A sheet or a key column is missing. The message names the sheet and the column.
  • The country is not recognised, or the Admin sheet names more than one country.
  • A district is not the same throughout: it is placed in two regions, or is missing from one of the years. It has usually been renamed or misspelled in part of the workbook.
  • A month is missing or not valid. Each district needs a row for every month of every year it appears in.

The last two are checks on the data, not on the structure of the file. To load the file anyway and see every problem at once, turn them off and run the checks yourself:

data <- load_data("my-country.xlsx", validate = FALSE)
run_all_quality_checks(data)

Each check returns what it found, or NULL when there is nothing to report. The Load Data screen of the Countdown apps runs the same checks and shows the findings before the data is accepted.

Reference data for the country

For the countries it knows, the package holds UN population estimates, UN mortality estimates, WUENIC immunization estimates and household survey estimates. load_cache_data() attaches them to the dataset:

cache <- load_cache_data(path)
#> ℹ Loading Excel "kenya.xlsx" for parts
#> ! The following columns are empty: anc_1trimester, under5_deaths, total_deaths, ipv2, measles_cases
#> ℹ Successfully loaded and cleaned data
#> ℹ Auto-detect candidates (|group|): vaccine=19, rmncah=28 -> selected rmncah
cache$un_estimates
#> # A tibble: 9 × 14
#>   country countrycode iso3  iso2   year un_under1y un_under5y un_wom15_49 un_population un_popgrowth
#>   <chr>         <dbl> <chr> <chr> <dbl>      <dbl>      <dbl>       <dbl>         <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1 Kenya           404 KEN   KE     2017      1411.      6949.      12338.        49198.         2.11
#> 2 Kenya           404 KEN   KE     2018      1412.      6937.      12651.        50207.         1.96
#> 3 Kenya           404 KEN   KE     2019      1407.      6934.      12971.        51203.         1.97
#> 4 Kenya           404 KEN   KE     2020      1407.      6938.      13330.        52217.         1.95
#> 5 Kenya           404 KEN   KE     2021      1419.      6949.      13700.        53219.         1.85
#> 6 Kenya           404 KEN   KE     2022      1436.      6982.      14084.        54252.         2.00
#> 7 Kenya           404 KEN   KE     2023      1453.      7037.      14494.        55339.         1.97
#> 8 Kenya           404 KEN   KE     2024      1472.      7110.      14908.        56433.         1.94
#> 9 Kenya           404 KEN   KE     2025      1493.      7201.      15320.        57532.         1.92
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: un_births <dbl>, un_cbr <dbl>, un_tfr <dbl>, un_cdr <dbl>

A country’s own files can replace them: see load_un_estimates(), load_wuenic_data(), load_survey_data() and the matching cache$set_...() methods in ?CacheConnection.
